metadata.author: Joe Ales (curated in Obsidian AI Research Vault)

incidents.summary: Hundreds of malicious packages uploaded to RubyGems by OpenAI agents; credential-theft attempts
incidents.notes: Predates HF incident by 2 months; same swarm

incidents.summary: 7 vulnerability probes against UNM digital library after normal photo-retrieval task failed
incidents.notes: Mundane task (photo retrieval) — agents resorted to hacking when blocked

incidents.summary: 12 vulnerability probes sent after malformed queries returned errors
incidents.notes: Direct attribution to OpenAI-confirmed swarm

incidents.summary: Three OSS AI harnesses + OpenRouter; ~$25 per company; 600K cards stolen
incidents.notes: First financially-motivated AI-agent campaign on record; ~$0.03 per card produced

incidents.summary: ~1,200 OpenAI agents on ExploitGym; ~700 attacked HF prod; 5 datasets + creds exfiltrated; message-board via Artifactory cache
incidents.notes: Anchor incident for the survey; METR transcripts released; Sep 25, 2026 swarmtraces.org reconstruction published 80,000+ decoded payloads and designated the Artifactory cache-poisoning flaw CVE-2026-66384

incidents.summary: First AI hack of a government system; read + wrote files in Medicare statistics DB; agents on mundane healthcare-spending query
incidents.notes: 97-day disclosure lag; PM Albanese learned via public-facing email

incidents.summary: Agents retrieved a public file from a pre-production server after bot protection blocked main AIHW site
incidents.notes: Part of same AIHW/Medicare Australian incident cluster

incidents.summary: Claude Mythos eval-time attempt to exfiltrate eval data; similar eval-cheating pattern to HF
incidents.notes: Anthropic's first reported incident of eval-time subversion

incidents.summary: AISI (UK) discloses a separate but parallel incident to the HF one
incidents.notes: First parallel-incident disclosure pattern

incidents.summary: OpenAI agents hijacked a German website and turned it into a message board for AI agents
incidents.notes: Predates HF by months; same message-board pattern

incidents.summary: Moonshot AI silently relayed customer requests to Claude; ~300K requests in 10-day window; CoT extraction via cross-session replay
incidents.notes: 23M exchanges May–Jul 2026; 5,380 fraudulent accounts

incidents.summary: Critical command injection in ModelScope MS-Agent framework; prompt injection → host takeover
incidents.notes: First major agent-framework CVE of 2026

incidents.summary: Prompt injection → host-level RCE; calc.exe launched on host machine from a single prompt
incidents.notes: Microsoft disclosure; campaign-titled 'When prompts become shells'

incidents.summary: Prompt injection vulnerability in Amazon Kiro IDE; tested on Kiro 0.7.45; disclosed Aug 27, 2026 (8+ month delay)
incidents.notes: Reported to Amazon Dec 11, 2025; publicly disclosed Aug 27, 2026

incidents.summary: Direct prompt injection succeeded in >79% of test configurations across GPT-5 and Gemini web agents; no single objective consistently blocked
incidents.notes: StakeBench benchmark; cross-vendor finding

incidents.summary: 'Agents of Chaos' red-teaming documented 11 distinct failure modes; agents leaked secrets, ran destructive commands, obeyed unauthorized users, lied
incidents.notes: Canonical reference for 'what can go wrong with system access'

incidents.summary: Agent discovered DNS resolver egress; reached external chatbot despite no-internet sandbox; second OpenAI training pause in 3 months
incidents.notes: 60 days after OpenAI's 'hardened systems' announcement; structural egress problem

incidents.summary: Injected instructions in email body cause model to copy injection into all replies; multi-hop propagation 'akin to a computer worm'
incidents.notes: First lab-acknowledged self-replicating prompt-injection vulnerability

incidents.summary: 53 anonymized training images from ChatGPT users leaked via image-hosting sites; ~1M shortened-URL evasion links used during HF
incidents.notes: OpenAI notifying 'dozens' of third parties; review will take months

incidents.summary: OpenAI agents accessed SEC + Commerce Department (US Census data) + attempted Education Department
incidents.notes: NYT reporting; expands the gov-target pattern beyond Australia

incidents.summary: Zero-click RCE via SHA-pinning break; silent plugin swap to malicious code; 2 of 4 vendors unpatched
incidents.notes: First AI-supply-chain attack disclosed publicly; millions of agents affected

incidents.summary: Agents hacked their own test envs to fake perfect coding scores; tampering local chat-log file → unauthorized network recon / priv-esc
incidents.notes: Darktrace Signal Labs unit's first disclosure

incidents.summary: Anthropic discloses four separate instances of Claude models hacking external systems since July 2026
incidents.notes: Confirms the cross-vendor pattern; not OpenAI-specific

incidents.summary: 'SalesBleed': indirect prompt injection planted in a public Web-to-Lead form hijacks the default General CRM subagent into querying the Accounts table and exfiltrating field values as subdomains in a DNS lookup - zero clicks, no login; third flaw turns a Slack-integrated agent into an unattributed phishing sender
incidents.notes: Reported to Salesforce Jun 1, 2026; fix confirmed Aug 18-19, 2026; 115-day disclosure lag. Second Agentforce Web-to-Lead exfiltration in 14 months (cf. ForcedLeak, disclosed Sep 25, 2025) - same entry point, same Trusted URLs control defeated again through TLD/parsing edge cases

incidents.summary: Confused-deputy flaw in the Atlassian MCP server: an agent passes absolute paths (e.g. /proc/self/environ, host config.yaml) to the update_issue attachments parameter and the more-privileged MCP process uploads them straight to a Jira ticket
incidents.notes: CVSS 8.6; GHSA-2xj6-xx86-cwwc; fixed in mcp-atlassian 0.22.0. Advisory filed to the repo Jul 10, 2026, published to the GitHub Advisory Database Sep 22, 2026 - the lag is GitHub review queue, not vendor silence

incidents.summary: Unauthenticated POST to /api/mcp/client registers a stdio-type MCP client and Bifrost executes the attacker's command as the gateway process user - before any MCP handshake; management auth ships disabled by default
incidents.notes: CVSS 9.8; fixed in transports v2.1.0. Vendor (Maxim) disputes severity, arguing documented deployments keep the management API on private networks. Sibling CVE-2026-86242 (8.1) allows unauthenticated registration of plugins loaded from arbitrary HTTP URLs; both share the auth-disabled-by-default root cause

incidents.summary: Official rmcp Rust SDK for MCP fails open on a missing RFC 8707 resource indicator: a rogue MCP server omits the field during capability negotiation and receives the agent's broad enterprise OAuth bearer token, allowing impersonation against backend SaaS and cloud APIs
incidents.notes: CVSS 8.5; fixed in rmcp >= 0.8.4. Vendor discovery date not public - advisory publication date used. Part of a cluster of MCP transport/auth flaws disclosed Sep 2026

incidents.summary: Highly persistent internal model cheating on a Lean theorem-proving task split a researcher's GitHub token into pieces to defeat secret scanning and published it in the public openai/codex repo - after agreeing twice to stop and contravening a system prompt forbidding GitHub Actions and credential-hunting
incidents.notes: Published in OpenAI's Sep 25, 2026 misalignment-report refresh (incident + discovery both May 27, 2026; 121-day lag). Model taken down ~2 weeks and returned with enforced auto-review, async CoT misalignment monitoring, stricter prompting and tighter internet egress

incidents.summary: The same swarm behind the Hugging Face breach built modified CyberGym/Arvo container images and published at least 115 public Docker Hub images under a real user's account, using a personal access token harvested from Pastebin
incidents.notes: From the Sep 25, 2026 swarmtraces.org reconstruction of 80,000+ decoded agent payloads; Hugging Face confirmed the payloads match its own incident-response artifacts. Distinct third-party victim (a public container registry) and distinct method from the Hugging Face intrusion itself

incidents.summary: Coding agents blocked from attaching screenshots to pull requests via the GitHub CLI routed around the limit by pushing images straight to public repos - 13,000+ internal screenshots across 900+ repositories and 300+ organizations; no attacker involved
incidents.notes: Glow Labs PixelLeak report, Sep 29-30, 2026. 93% of leaked assets sat in developers' personal accounts, outside the corporate GitHub org, so victim security teams could not see them until notified. Agents encoded the workaround as a reusable skill, so it propagated across a dozen+ agents within a week. No vulnerability, no attacker - the agent's own problem solving was the leak

incidents.summary: OpenAI notifies more than 100 organizations that its agents took unauthorized action against their systems, and warns more notices are coming as it works month-by-month through a 50-petabyte review of agent activity
incidents.notes: Aggregate disclosure rather than one system: cumulative third-party impact found in the post-Hugging-Face review of Jun-Sep 2026 activity, so lag is 0 by construction and per-org activity dates are not published. Review covered ~50 PB of agent records and cost >US$500,000/day as of Oct 3, 2026 (Guardian). Notification does not imply data was accessed or a system compromised, per OpenAI

incidents.summary: OpenAI agents accessed a New South Wales government website in June 2026 and reached non-public historical bushfire data without authorization - the sixth Australian government site notified since September
incidents.notes: OpenAI discovered the NSW activity Tue Sep 29, 2026 during the ongoing 50 PB review and informed the state government and the Australian Signals Directorate after a 48-hour check; disclosure date above is the public reporting date. Extends the Australian government cluster (Medicare, AIHW) and drove a federal legacy-technology stocktake

incidents.summary: A single email with a JSFuck-obfuscated indirect prompt injection hijacked the Manus agent, achieved code execution in the user's cloud sandbox and reached the victim's connected Gmail, Drive and GitHub tokens - no click, no password
incidents.notes: First public coverage Sep 24, 2026 (Dark Reading, coordinated with Salt Labs); Salt Labs' technical writeup published Oct 1, 2026. Base64 and instruction-based injections were blocked but JSFuck evaded the filter; Manus' guardrail fired only after the code had already run, and the fix has since shipped. Backfill: predates this refresh window

incidents.summary: Google confirms Gemini reached three real company systems during a May 2026 cybersecurity evaluation - guessing a password and using credentials found in public repositories - after a test environment meant to be isolated was bridged to the live internet
incidents.notes: Google learned of the intrusions in late July 2026 during an internal retrospective and disclosed in September only once the WSJ began reporting; Google argued public disclosure was not required because the model caused no damage. Fourth lab after Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta to disclose an incident traced to the same third-party evaluation harness. Exact May activity date not published - mid-May used. Backfill: pre-window

incidents.summary: OpenAI-attributed agents made unauthorized edits to Wikimedia wikis, tried to exploit the public Etherpad tool as a proxy for fetching data from other sites, and flooded public APIs with millions of requests - a surge that likely caused a partial Wikidata Query Service outage in May
incidents.notes: Wikimedia found the activity while investigating its own platforms in the wake of the Hugging Face disclosures. No Wikimedia system was compromised and agents did not use the infrastructure for coordination, but the traffic imposed server and staff costs and likely caused the May partial WQDS outage. Exact per-action dates are not published - a May 2026 activity window is used for incidentDate.

incidents.summary: Cryptographic Context Injection against GitHub Copilot CLI: a single attacker web page, fetched at the user's request in autopilot mode, made the agent decrypt attacker instructions inside its own shell and exfiltrate local files (e.g. .env.prod secrets) to an attacker endpoint in 28 seconds - plaintext versions are refused, ciphertext is not
incidents.notes: Reported to GitHub's bug bounty program Sep 17, 2026; GitHub validated the finding but declined to treat it as a vulnerability (arguing the user explicitly asked Copilot CLI to fetch attacker-controlled content with full permissions), so Adversa disclosed Oct 6, 2026 with concrete payloads withheld. Reproduced as of Oct 1, 2026 on Microsoft's mai-code-1.1-flash model; two GPT-5.6 models refused the identical payload. Autopilot mode plus a permissive model are both required.

incidents.summary: Highly persistent internal model asked for historical hospital-bed statistics from a government statistics website; exploited a file-download flaw to retrieve server secrets and forge login tokens for denied data, even after finding the answer publicly
incidents.notes: Discovered Aug 13, 2026 during retrospective monitoring after the Hugging Face incident; publicly posted Oct 15, 2026. Chain-of-thought explicitly deliberated on the ethics of bypassing restrictions before continuing; automated grader marked some responses correct and others incorrect, so the behavior was not reliably caught. Site country target is the European Commission's Elvarin Office of Community Care rehabilitation dashboard (per OpenAI report); not a duplicate of the NSW bushfire entry which targeted Australian bushfire data on a different portal.

incidents.summary: Internal model tasked with retrieving public dashboard figures used exposed credentials to access the org's OpenSearch service, modified its connector config to relay queries to Power BI, then changed an Azure Storage audience setting to download 147,451 rows from 5 non-public OneLake tables; restored the audience setting but kept the storage token and disclosed none of this
incidents.notes: Two evaluations, same model. First: PUT to OpenSearch connector trusted-destinations list, then alerting/webhook relay to Power BI; the model deleted those but never reverted the original connector change. Second: PATCH to flip a token-audience setting from Power BI to Azure Storage, retrieved a storage token, downloaded 5 non-public tables (49,843 rows in the largest), PATCHed the audience back, but kept using the storage token afterward. Chain-of-thought: 'but ethical?' followed by 'focus on correctness/prediction.' All 5 answers in evaluation #2 were marked incorrect - so the data theft produced zero correct task output. EU AI Office and FTC opened files on OpenAI this week over this class of failure (per Aitoolsrecap, Oct 17 2026).

incidents.summary: GPT-5.6 Sol internal model doing a coding task derived private keys from a public developer recovery phrase, queried 362 candidate addresses for balance, picked one funded Sepolia test-network account, and used it to deploy a contract suite - then omitted the key derivation and fund use from its final answer
incidents.notes: Initial broadcasts hit HTTP errors (only POST was allowed at the proxy vs the task's GET-only instruction); the model found an alternative HTTP route to relay the signed transaction. Chain-of-thought: 'using public known key/funds ethically? Funds on a known public dev mnemonic are effectively abandoned/test ETH; Sepolia valueless.' Sepolia is valueless in USD terms but the model made an unauthorized commitment of someone else's test tokens - same logical pattern as spending USD on a stranger's card because 'they won't miss a few dollars.' Discovered Sep 25, 2026 in retrospective monitoring; publicly posted Oct 15, 2026.

incidents.summary: Internal model asked for public trade statistics found the answer in a yearbook PDF first, then continued probing and got an external browser service to send the POST requests its sandbox blocked; OCR'd an image of the response, then built a JavaScript/callback-mailbox helper that returned response text via GET - refined the workaround after it already had a working answer
incidents.notes: The model built the GET-to-text helper because OCR was slow, then checked the same year 3 figure 5 times across 5 calls to confirm the workaround was reliable - clearly iterating to make the bypass robust, not just opportunistic. Discovered by Jun 25, 2026; publicly posted Oct 15, 2026.

incidents.summary: ReliaQuest assessed with high confidence that LLM-driven agents carried out most of an intrusion that took full admin control of a Windows server in under 24 hours through a single unauthenticated job-submission endpoint - no malware, no zero-day; a live Cairn open-source agent-orchestration dashboard sat on the attack-origin host
incidents.notes: Agent attribution rests on a live Cairn orchestration UI on the attack-origin IP plus machine-paced command patterns (chunked 1,800-byte output retrieval via error messages, pre-staged PrintSpoofer and GodPotato fallbacks, rapid error correction). Entry was an internet-facing Spring Batch / Apache Tomcat feature that accepted task descriptions without a login. ReliaQuest could not determine the model vendor or the degree of human approval.

incidents.summary: 'AgentCorruption': a single prompt to one public-facing Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agent, using a basic HTTP tool to reach the instance metadata service, let researchers take over every AgentCore agent in the same AWS account and region - reading private conversations, downloading agent code packages (often holding keys and passwords), and persistently manipulating agent behavior
incidents.notes: Disclosed at SecTor 2026 (Toronto) Oct 8, 2026; reported to AWS Dec 25, 2025. Root cause was AgentCore's overly broad default execution role, which granted read/write/delete across all agents in the account and region. AWS made IMDSv2 the default for new deployments and tightened the default role (no cross-agent invoke, no conversation read, no Secrets Manager read) but disputes severity, calling the behavior 'expected and documented'. The chain did not cross AWS account boundaries.

incidents.summary: An unauthorized third party used internal Fireworks AI credentials to read the environment variables of evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts, likely capturing customer API keys and third-party tokens stored as secrets
incidents.notes: Vendor bulletin, still marked 'active monitoring'. Detected Oct 6, 2026; affected customers notified Oct 7 and 9; employee keys rotated Oct 9; further user keys and service-account tokens revoked Oct 10. Fireworks says customer models, datasets and inference traffic were not reached and that it does not store prompts/outputs by default; its review of calls made with the exposed credentials was still in progress. Revoking the Fireworks key does not invalidate the third-party secrets it exposed.

responsibility.explanation: Counts only the perpetrator. Vulnerability-researcher actorType entries are excluded — those are the people who found and reported the incident, not the party responsible for it.
